title: Clean derived open units respect actual exchange and profinite action families
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and use the pulled-back rings $\Lambda_W=p_W^*\Lambda$, internal modules on small pro-etale sites, and the specified adjunctions $g^*\dashv Rg_*$ on ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion, $g:X'\to X$ any scheme morphism, $V'=X'\times_XV$, $j':V'\hookrightarrow X'$, and $g_V:V'\to V$. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ write $\eta_K:K\to Rj_*j^*K$ and $\eta'_{g^*K}:g^*K\to Rj'_*j'^*g^*K$ for the actual units. Let
$$b_{g,K}:g^*Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow Rj'_*j'^*g^*K$$
be the adjunct of $g_V^*\varepsilon_{j^*K}$, inserting the canonical pullback-composition comparison. Then
$$b_{g,K}\circ g^*\eta_K=\eta'_{g^*K}.$$
If both units are invertible, then $b_{g,K}$ is invertible and
$$g^*(\eta_K^{-1})=(\eta'_{g^*K})^{-1}\circ b_{g,K}.$$
For a morphism $u:K\to L$ of objects with invertible units one has $Rj_*j^*u\circ\eta_K=\eta_L\circ u$ and $u\circ\eta_K^{-1}=\eta_L^{-1}\circ Rj_*j^*u$.
These equations also give the following precise family statement. Let $X$ be affine, let $Q$ be profinite, and use $X[Q]$ and $V[Q]$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Let $a:X[Q]\to X$ be a morphism with $a^{-1}(V)=V[Q]$, let $\operatorname{pr}:X[Q]\to X$ be the projection, and supply an isomorphism $\rho:a^*K\cong\operatorname{pr}^*K$. If the units for $K$ on $X$ and for $\operatorname{pr}^*K$ on $X[Q]$ are invertible, the exchanges for $a$ and $\operatorname{pr}$ are invertible and
$$Rj_{Q,*}j_Q^*\rho\circ b_{a,K}\circ a^*\eta_K=b_{\operatorname{pr},K}\circ\operatorname{pr}^*\eta_K\circ\rho,$$
where $j_Q:V[Q]\hookrightarrow X[Q]$. The inverse-unit action equation is $\rho\circ(\eta_{a^*K})^{-1}=(\eta_{\operatorname{pr}^*K})^{-1}\circ Rj_{Q,*}j_Q^*\rho$. These are equalities of morphisms on $X[Q]$ itself. They include an individual open-preserving automorphism with its supplied module action ($Q=*$), and apply with $X[P]$ in place of $X$ for any profinite $P$. No pointwise criterion on $Q$ or cleanness assumption on unrelated objects is imposed.

proof.text: Use the specified ordinary unbounded adjunctions of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $L=j^*$, $R=Rj_*$, $L\prime=j\prime{}^*$, $R\prime=Rj\prime_*$, $G=g^*$ and $H=g_V^*$. Composition of pullbacks [prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp], applied to the equality $g\circ j\prime=j\circ g_V$, supplies the natural isomorphism $\alpha:L\prime G\xrightarrow{\sim}HL$. Thus the target identification is $R\prime H L K\xrightarrow{R\prime(\alpha_K^{-1})}R\prime L\prime GK$. No base-change isomorphism for direct image is being assumed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: the ambient derived adjunctions and pullback square

proof.text: By the mate formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], at an object $M$ of $D(V)$ the unnormalized exchange is $m_M=R\prime(H\varepsilon_M\circ\alpha_{RM})\circ\eta\prime_{GRM}$. Hence the actual map in the statement is $b_{g,K}=R\prime(\alpha_K^{-1})\circ m_{LK}$. Naturality of the target unit from [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives $$m_{LK}\circ G\eta_K=R\prime(H\varepsilon_{LK}\circ\alpha_{RLK}\circ L\prime G\eta_K)\circ\eta\prime_{GK}.$$ Naturality of $\alpha$ replaces $\alpha_{RLK}\circ L\prime G\eta_K$ by $HL\eta_K\circ\alpha_K$. The source triangle identity $\varepsilon_{LK}\circ L\eta_K=1_{LK}$, also supplied by that adjunction node, reduces this to $R\prime(\alpha_K)\circ\eta\prime_{GK}$. Composing with $R\prime(\alpha_K^{-1})$ proves $b_{g,K}\circ g^*\eta_K=\eta\prime_{g^*K}$ with exactly the specified comparison.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), actual counit-mate construction; unit and triangle calculation using Tag 0037

proof.text: If $\eta_K$ and $\eta\prime_{g^*K}$ are invertible, the preceding identity gives $b_{g,K}=\eta\prime_{g^*K}\circ g^*(\eta_K^{-1})$. Functoriality sends the two inverse equations for $\eta_K$ to inverse equations for its image. Thus an explicit inverse of $b_{g,K}$ is $g^*\eta_K\circ(\eta\prime_{g^*K})^{-1}$. Multiplying the displayed formula for $b_{g,K}$ on the left by $(\eta\prime_{g^*K})^{-1}$ gives the asserted inverse-unit exchange equation.

Apply the unit naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to $u:K\to L$: $RL(u)\circ\eta_K=\eta_L\circ u$. If the two units are invertible, compose on the left with $\eta_L^{-1}$ and on the right with $\eta_K^{-1}$. Associativity and the inverse equations give $u\circ\eta_K^{-1}=\eta_L^{-1}\circ RL(u)$, proving both morphism-naturality assertions.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), paragraph after the definition: functoriality of the adjunction maps

proof.text: For the family put $A=a^*K$, $B=\operatorname{pr}^*K$, $T=Rj_{Q,*}j_Q^*$ and let $e_C:C\to TC$ be its unit. Naturality from [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] at the supplied isomorphism $\rho:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ says $T\rho\circ e_A=e_B\circ\rho$. Since $e_B$ is invertible by hypothesis, this gives $e_A=(T\rho)^{-1}\circ e_B\circ\rho$, with inverse $\rho^{-1}\circ e_B^{-1}\circ T\rho$. This also proves directly $\rho\circ e_A^{-1}=e_B^{-1}\circ T\rho$. Thus the missing unit is invertible using only the supplied isomorphism, with no cleanness assertion about other objects.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), naturality at the supplied family isomorphism

proof.text: By [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], $V[Q]$ is the base change of $X[Q]$ along $V\to X$: this follows by pasting the two fibre products in the definition. The projection therefore has inverse image $V[Q]$; the same is assumed for $a$. Apply steps 2 and 3 to these two squares. Both exchanges are invertible, and $b_{a,K}\circ a^*\eta_K=e_A$, $b_{\operatorname{pr},K}\circ\operatorname{pr}^*\eta_K=e_B$. Substitution into the naturality equation of step 5 gives exactly $$T\rho\circ b_{a,K}\circ a^*\eta_K=b_{\operatorname{pr},K}\circ\operatorname{pr}^*\eta_K\circ\rho.$$ Step 5 already gives the claimed inverse-unit action equation. Every map and equality lies in the derived category on $X[Q]$ itself.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted whole-profinite-family compatibility: substitution of the actual units

proof.text: The preceding argument used no property of individual points of $Q$. For $Q=*$, the definition [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] has $LC(*,\mathbf Z)=\mathbf Z$, so $X[*]=X$, and an open-preserving automorphism with its supplied module isomorphism is a special case. Moreover steps 1--6 never used affineness of the base scheme: they used only its adjunctions, pullback square, the supplied isomorphism and the two assumed invertible units. Thus they apply to the scheme $X[P]$ of [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] and its pulled-back open for every profinite $P$, under exactly the same supplied-unit hypotheses. This proves the final assertions without any pointwise detection criterion.
